title: Pide
subtitle: Turkish boat-shaped flatbread with spiced mince and egg
excerpt: Soft yeasted dough shaped into an open boat, filled with spiced minced lamb and a cracked egg, then baked until the sides are puffed and golden and the filling is just set.
sourceNotes: Turkish Black Sea and Anatolian pide tradition. Synthesised from multiple Turkish baking and street food sources.

recipe.batchNotes: Make extra dough and filling and bake in batches. The filling can be made up to a day ahead.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough can rest overnight in the fridge after the first rise. Bring back to room temperature before shaping.

content.text: Pide are Turkish flatbreads shaped like a boat, with the edges pinched up to hold a filling. The egg goes in for the last few minutes of baking so it sets just right. Watch the oven towards the end since the filling can overcook quickly.

items.prepNote: for the filling, one per pide

content.text: Mix the flour, yeast, and salt. Add the water and olive oil. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled.

Cook the onion in a dry pan for 3 minutes. Add the lamb mince and cook for 5 minutes, breaking it up. Add the tomato, peppers, paprika-sweet, tomato puree, and black pepper. Cook for 4 more minutes until the liquid reduces. Season and leave to cool slightly.
Heat the oven to 220C. Place two baking trays in the oven to heat.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces. Roll each into an oval about 30cm long and 15cm wide. Transfer to sheets of baking paper.
Divide the filling between the ovals, spreading it in the centre and leaving a 2cm border. Fold the long edges up over the filling and pinch the ends together to form a boat shape.
Brush the exposed dough edges with the beaten egg. Slide onto the hot baking trays. Bake for 12 minutes.

Pull the trays out. Make a small well in each filling and crack in one egg. Return to the oven for 4 to 5 minutes until the egg white is just set. Brush the crust with melted butter and serve straight away.

items.symptom: The boat shape opened up during baking.
items.cause: The ends were not pinched firmly enough.
items.fix: Press and seal the pointed ends firmly before baking. A small roll of foil at each end can hold the shape if needed.

items.symptom: The egg is overcooked and hard.
items.cause: It went in too early, or the oven is too hot.
items.fix: Add the egg in the final 4 minutes only. The white should be set but the yolk still a little soft.

items.symptom: The base is raw in the middle.
items.cause: The filling was too wet, or the tray was not preheated.
items.fix: Drain excess liquid from the filling before spreading. Always preheat the baking trays.
